steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our text-to-3D generation paper (HiFA). Cover the background on text-to-3D and score distillation, the problems we see with timestep sampling and with NeRF geometry and texture in single-stage optimization, our proposed fixes, and a summary of contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Text-to-3D generation: applications, early 3D generative work, data scarcity
- Lifting pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models to 3D; SDS and follow-ups
- Our approach: single-stage SDS + NeRF; latent and image space distillation; timestep annealing
- Difficulty of detailed single-stage generation; limits of mesh and two-stage approaches
- Two NeRF techniques: z-variance regularization, kernel smoothing for importance sampling
- Summary of contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Text-to-3D background
  - create 3D assets from text; applications: digital content generation, film-making, Virtual Reality (VR) (cite)
  - early: unconditional 3D asset generation; explicit representations e.g. meshes (cite), implicit e.g. fields (cite)
  - then conditional 3D generative models, e.g. text-based guidance (cite)
  - limited to relatively simple assets: scarcity of large-scale annotated 3D datasets
- Lifting 2D models to 3D
  - ample image datasets + success of text-to-image generation
  - optimize a 3D representation using pre-trained text-to-image models giving denoising score for rendered images (cite)
  - one prior work (cite): loss from distilling text-to-image diffusion model; minimize KL divergence between family of Gaussians from forward diffusion and denoising scores from pre-trained model
  - Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) + NeRF -> 3D assets from text prompts
  - follow-ups: two-stage optimization (cite), changes to SDS formulation (cite), disentangling geometry and appearance (cite)
- Our approach
  - revisit SDS + NeRFs, photo-realistic high-quality text-to-3D through single-stage optimization
  - distill score in diffusion model's latent and image spaces -> enhanced supervision
  - diffusion prior efficacy limited in previous works (cite) when timesteps (noise levels in denoising score matching) randomly sampled
  - near end of training NeRF almost determined; large random timestep -> denoised image distinct/unrelated to input rendering -> inconsistent distillation, compromised NeRF optimization
  - fix: timestep annealing, timestep inversely correlated with square root of number of training iterations
  - improves generation quality; square root beats linear and cosine ratios
- Single-stage detail is hard
  - explicit (meshes): struggle with intricate topology, e.g. holes
  - implicit (cite): cloudy geometry, flickering textures; Moiré patterns for detailed geometry like human bodies (cite)
  - prior works (cite) use two-stage: explicit representation e.g. Deep Marching Tetrahedra (DMTet) (cite) extracts textured meshes from implicit one in stage 1, fine-tuned in stage 2
  - meshes lose detailed appearance like fur -> tradeoff to avoid
  - we keep NeRF flexibility and photo-realism, single-stage training
- Technique 1: z-variance regularization
  - cloudy geometry -> minimize variance of sampled z-coordinates along NeRF rays
  - crisper geometric surfaces, mitigates cloudiness
  - beats alternative spatial regularization from previous methods (cite)
- Technique 2: kernel smoothing
  - flickering / shimmer: inaccurate importance sampling weights across rendering views
  - existing fixes (more sampling points; separate density networks for coarse and refined stage) cost more compute
  - ours: kernel smoothing for coarse-to-fine importance sampling, no extra computational cost
  - inspired by integrated positional encoding for points in a cone, for aliasing in single image view (cite); our goal: flickering across multiple views
  - kernel refines PDF estimated in coarse stage -> more sampling near asset surface in refined stage
  - improves fidelity of importance sampling
- Contributions, two components: (1) 3D representation, (2) optimization
  - score distillation in latent and image space; timestep annealing
  - regularization on variance of z-coordinates along rays -> sharp geometry, single stage
  - kernel smoothing refining PDF estimation -> addresses flickering
  - together: address shortcomings, better 3D synthesis

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
The task of automatic text-to-3D generation is to create 3D assets from a text description. It has received a lot of attention because it has many applications, such as digital content generation, film-making, and Virtual Reality (VR). Early work in this area focused on unconditional 3D asset generation, and tried different 3D representations, both explicit ones like meshes and implicit ones like fields. After this the field moved to conditional 3D generative models, for example with text-based guidance. But these studies were limited to fairly simple 3D assets, mainly because there are not many large-scale annotated 3D datasets.

Since there are plenty of image datasets and text-to-image generation has been so successful, it became possible to lift pre-trained text-to-image models to the 3D domain. In particular, recent studies optimize a 3D representation for an asset by using pre-trained text-to-image generative models that provide a denoising score for rendered images. One prior work proposed a loss that comes from distilling a text-to-image diffusion model. It minimized the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between a family of Gaussian distributions based on the forward diffusion process and the denoising scores from the pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model. This Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) method, combined with a NeRF, makes it possible to generate 3D assets from text prompts. Later research improved the generation quality in different ways, for example two-stage optimization frameworks, changes to the original SDS formulation, and disentangling geometry and appearance.

In this work we look again at combining the SDS approach with NeRFs, with the goal of photo-realistic and high-quality text-to-3D generation in a single-stage optimization. Different from existing text-to-3D work, we distill the score in both the latent space and the image space of the text-to-image diffusion model, which gives stronger supervision. We also observe that the diffusion prior is not used effectively in previous works when the timesteps (also called noise levels in denoising score matching) are sampled randomly during optimization. Near the end of training, the NeRF is almost fixed in representing a particular 3D asset. So if a large timestep is sampled at random, the diffusion model produces a denoised image that is distinct from and unrelated to the input rendering. The distillation from the diffusion model is then inconsistent and the NeRF optimization suffers. To fix this we introduce timestep annealing, where the timestep in the forward diffusion process is inversely correlated with the square root of the number of training iterations. Our experiments show that this timestep annealing improves generation quality, and that the square root annealing is consistently better than other annealing methods like linear and cosine ratios.

- Single-stage detail is hard
  - explicit (meshes): struggle with intricate topology, e.g. holes
  - implicit (cite): cloudy geometry, flickering textures; Moiré patterns for detailed geometry like human bodies (cite)
  - prior works (cite) use two-stage: explicit representation e.g. Deep Marching Tetrahedra (DMTet) (cite) extracts textured meshes from implicit one in stage 1, fine-tuned in stage 2
  - meshes lose detailed appearance like fur -> tradeoff to avoid
  - we keep NeRF flexibility and photo-realism, single-stage training

- Technique 1: z-variance regularization
  - cloudy geometry -> minimize variance of sampled z-coordinates along NeRF rays
  - crisper geometric surfaces, mitigates cloudiness
  - beats alternative spatial regularization from previous methods (cite)

- Technique 2: kernel smoothing
  - flickering / shimmer: inaccurate importance sampling weights across rendering views
  - existing fixes (more sampling points; separate density networks for coarse and refined stage) cost more compute
  - ours: kernel smoothing for coarse-to-fine importance sampling, no extra computational cost
  - inspired by integrated positional encoding for points in a cone, for aliasing in single image view (cite); our goal: flickering across multiple views
  - kernel refines PDF estimated in coarse stage -> more sampling near asset surface in refined stage
  - improves fidelity of importance sampling

- Contributions, two components: (1) 3D representation, (2) optimization
  - score distillation in latent and image space; timestep annealing
  - regularization on variance of z-coordinates along rays -> sharp geometry, single stage
  - kernel smoothing refining PDF estimation -> addresses flickering
  - together: address shortcomings, better 3D synthesis

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
The task of automatic text-to-3D generation is to create 3D assets from a text description. It has received a lot of attention because it has many applications, such as digital content generation, film-making, and Virtual Reality (VR). Early work in this area focused on unconditional 3D asset generation, and tried different 3D representations, both explicit ones like meshes and implicit ones like fields. After this the field moved to conditional 3D generative models, for example with text-based guidance. But these studies were limited to fairly simple 3D assets, mainly because there are not many large-scale annotated 3D datasets.

Since there are plenty of image datasets and text-to-image generation has been so successful, it became possible to lift pre-trained text-to-image models to the 3D domain. In particular, recent studies optimize a 3D representation for an asset by using pre-trained text-to-image generative models that provide a denoising score for rendered images. One prior work proposed a loss that comes from distilling a text-to-image diffusion model. It minimized the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between a family of Gaussian distributions based on the forward diffusion process and the denoising scores from the pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model. This Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) method, combined with a NeRF, makes it possible to generate 3D assets from text prompts. Later research improved the generation quality in different ways, for example two-stage optimization frameworks, changes to the original SDS formulation, and disentangling geometry and appearance.

In this work we look again at combining the SDS approach with NeRFs, with the goal of photo-realistic and high-quality text-to-3D generation in a single-stage optimization. Different from existing text-to-3D work, we distill the score in both the latent space and the image space of the text-to-image diffusion model, which gives stronger supervision. We also observe that the diffusion prior is not used effectively in previous works when the timesteps (also called noise levels in denoising score matching) are sampled randomly during optimization. Near the end of training, the NeRF is almost fixed in representing a particular 3D asset. So if a large timestep is sampled at random, the diffusion model produces a denoised image that is distinct from and unrelated to the input rendering. The distillation from the diffusion model is then inconsistent and the NeRF optimization suffers. To fix this we introduce timestep annealing, where the timestep in the forward diffusion process is inversely correlated with the square root of the number of training iterations. Our experiments show that this timestep annealing improves generation quality, and that the square root annealing is consistently better than other annealing methods like linear and cosine ratios.

Also, it is hard to generate a detailed 3D asset with single-stage optimization. Explicit 3D representations like meshes have trouble capturing intricate topology, for example shapes with holes. Implicit 3D representations can give cloudy geometry and flickering textures. For example, Moiré patterns are noticable when NeRFs are used to represent very detailed 3D geometries like human bodies. Because of this, prior works used two-stage optimization. In these approaches, explicit 3D representations such as Deep Marching Tetrahedra (DMTet) are used to extract textured meshes from the implicit representations in the first stage, and these are then fine-tuned in the second stage to get high-quality geometry. But the mesh representations lose the ability to produce detailed appearances like fur, and we want to avoid this tradeoff. Instead, we want to keep the flexibility and photo-realism of the NeRF representation and still get high-quality text-to-3D generation with single-stage training.

For this we propose two techniques to improve NeRF optimization. The first one targets the cloudy geometry problem in NeRFs: we propose a variance regularization that minimizes the variance of the sampled z-coordinates along NeRF rays. We see that this lets NeRFs represent crisp geometrical surfaces more accurately, so the cloudiness problem is reduced. We also check that our z-variance regularization does better than the alternative spatial regularization used in previous methods.

The second issue is texture flickering, or shimmer effects, which often come from inaccurate estimates of the importance sampling weights across different rendering views. Existing solutions, like using more sampling points along the rays or using separate density estimation networks for the coarse and refined stages, need more computation. We instead propose a kernel smoothing technique for coarse-to-fine importance sampling along NeRF rays that does not increase the computational cost. The idea is inspired by the integrated positional encoding for spatial points inside a cone, which was proposed before to deal with aliasing in a single image view. In our case the goal is to reduce flickering across multiple views. We use a kernel to refine the probability density function (PDF) estimated along a ray in the coarse sampling stage, so that the refined stage samples more thoroughly near the asset surface regions. This technique clearly improves the fidelity of importance sampling.

Our technical contributions are for two important components of text-to-3D generation, (1) 3D representation and (2) optimization:

- • We propose score distillation in both the latent and the image space of the pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models, to get photo-realistic and highly-detailed text-to-3D generation. We also introduce a timestep annealing approach for score distillation from text-to-image diffusion models.

- • We present a regularization method on the variance of z-coordinates along NeRF rays, to get sharp geometry with single-stage training.

- • We propose a kernel smoothing technique that refines the PDF estimation in coarse-to-fine importance sampling, to deal with flickering in NeRFs.

Together, we show how these modifications address existing shortcomings and improve the quality of 3D synthesis.

The availability of ample image datasets and the success of text-to-image generation have paved the way for lifting pre-trained text-to-image models to the 3D domain. Specifically, recent studies optimize a 3D representation for an asset using pre-trained text-to-image generative models that provide a denoising score for rendered images [11,12,13,14,15,1,16,2,17]. [13] proposed a loss from the distillation of a text-to-image diffusion model, minimizing the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between a family of Gaussian distributions based on the forward diffusion process and the denoising scores obtained from the pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model. This Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) method, combined with a NeRF, enables 3D asset generation from given text prompts. Subsequent research has improved generation quality through various approaches, including two-stage optimization frameworks [1,16,17,18], alterations to the original SDS formulation [15,17], and the disentanglement of geometry and appearance [2].

In this work, we revisit the integration of the SDS approach with NeRFs, aiming at photo-realistic and high-quality text-to-3D generation through a single-stage optimization. In contrast to existing text-to-3D work, we distill the score in both the latent and image spaces of the text-to-image diffusion model for enhanced supervision. Moreover, we observe that the efficacy of the diffusion prior is limited in previous works [13,1] when timesteps (also referred to as noise levels in denoising score matching) are randomly sampled during optimization. Toward the end of training, the NeRF is almost determined in representing a particular 3D asset, so randomly sampling a large timestep drives the diffusion model to produce a denoised image that is distinct and unrelated to the original input rendering. This leads to inconsistent distillation from the diffusion model and compromised optimization of NeRFs. To address this, we introduce a timestep annealing approach in which the timestep in the forward diffusion process inversely correlates with the square root of the number of training iterations. Our empirical analysis shows that timestep annealing effectively enhances generation quality, and that square root annealing consistently outperforms other annealing methods, such as linear and cosine ratios.

Moreover, generating a detailed 3D asset through single-stage optimization is challenging. Explicit 3D representations, such as meshes, struggle to capture intricate topology, such as those with holes, while implicit 3D representations [19,20] may lead to cloudy geometry and flickering textures. For instance, Moiré patterns are noticable when NeRFs are employed to represent highly detailed 3D geometries like human bodies [21]. Prior works [1,17] therefore adopted two-stage optimization techniques, in which explicit 3D representations such as Deep Marching Tetrahedra (DMTet) [22] are used to extract textured meshes from the implicit representations in the first stage and are then fine-tuned in the second stage to capture high-quality geometry. However, these mesh representations lose the ability to produce detailed appearances such as fur – a tradeoff we wish to avoid. Instead, we aim to keep the flexibility and photo-realism of the NeRF representation while achieving high-quality text-to-3D generation through single-stage training.

To this end, we propose two techniques to advance NeRF optimization. First, to address the cloudy geometry issue in NeRFs, we propose a variance regularization that minimizes the variance of sampled z-coordinates distributed along NeRF rays. We observe that this enables NeRFs to represent crisp geometrical surfaces more accurately, effectively mitigating the cloudiness issue. We also verify that our z-variance regularization outperforms the alternative spatial regularization proposed in previous methods [23].

Second, texture flickering or shimmer effects often result from inaccurate estimates of the importance sampling weights across different rendering views. Existing solutions, such as increasing the number of sampling points along the rays or deploying separate density estimation networks for the coarse and refined stages, increase computational demands. Instead, we propose a kernel smoothing technique tailored for coarse-to-fine importance sampling along NeRF rays without increasing the computational cost. It is inspired by the integrated positional encoding for spatial points within a cone, previously proposed to tackle aliasing in a single image view [24]; in our case, the goal is to mitigate flickering across multiple views. Specifically, we use a kernel to refine the probability density function (PDF) estimated along a ray in the coarse sampling stage, which enables more comprehensive sampling near asset surface regions in the refined stage. This notably enhances the fidelity of importance sampling.

We summarize our technical contributions for two crucial components of text-to-3D generation, (1) 3D representation and (2) optimization, as follows:

- • To achieve photo-realistic and highly-detailed text-to-3D generation, we propose score distillation in both the latent and image space of pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models, and we introduce a timestep annealing approach for score distillation from text-to-image diffusion models.

- • To achieve sharp geometry through single-stage training, we present a regularization method applied to the variance of z-coordinates along NeRF rays.

- • To address flickering in NeRFs, we propose a kernel smoothing technique that refines the PDF estimation in coarse-to-fine importance sampling.

Taken together, we show how these modifications address existing shortcomings and improve the quality of 3D synthesis.
